content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [[-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised return value (array of triplets). Each triplet should be an array of three integers, sorted ascending. The judge will normalize results by sorting triplets and the list of triplets before comparison.

The only triplet [0,0,0] sums to zero.

content.problemStatement:
With an integer array `nums`, output all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets. Each triplet in the returned list should be sorted in non-decreasing order; the judge will normalize and sort the list of triplets before comparison so output ordering is not significant.

Aim for an algorithm that runs in O(n^2) time on average and uses O(1) extra space (excluding the space required for the output). A standard approach is to sort the array and use a two-pointer scan for each fixed first element.

notes: Before comparing outputs, the judge normalizes both expected and submitted outputs by: 1) sorting each triplet in non-decreasing order, 2) sorting the list of triplets lexicographically, then performing an equality check.

Generator-style testcases (type=gen) are expanded by the judge harness at runtime. For generator tests the harness must compute expected outputs deterministically using the same seed and generator logic and compare submission outputs after normalization.
All concrete testcases compare the normalized triplet lists for equality.

solution.approach: Sort the array and for each index i (as the first element) use a two-pointer scan (left, right) on the suffix to find pairs that sum to -nums[i]. Skip duplicate values for the fixed element and skip duplicates when moving left/right pointers to avoid duplicate triplets. This yields O(n^2) time after sorting and O(1) extra auxiliary space (excluding output).
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) on average (sorting O(n log n) + two-pointer scans O(n^2))
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space (excluding the space required for the output)
